# Knowledge, collaborative vectors, and semantic codes: how does the same content enter different recommender interfaces?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/recommendation/content-semantic-ids.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 60 topic entries / 4 representative comparisons

KAR generates external knowledge for an existing recommender. NoteLLM learns a searchable compressed state from co-reading. Dual-purpose SID uses compact codes for both identity and content reconstruction. FineSID transfers fine-grained tokens and a complete interaction backbone across stages. Their alignment signals, compressed objects, and inherited states differ even when they all use LLMs or SIDs.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Ask what actually gets transferred

KAR transfers features produced from generated knowledge via an adapter. NoteLLM transfers a collaboratively trained compressed vector. Dual-purpose SID transfers a discrete identity that reconstructs content. FineSID transfers shared predictor parameters and normalization state. Adding a random codebook to an existing CTR model reproduces neither KAR's knowledge source nor FineSID's stage inheritance. A token interface does not make them equivalent.

Sources: [Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en.md) · [NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en.md) · [Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en.md) · [Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en.md)

### Measure content fidelity and recommendation relevance separately

Dual-purpose SID reconstruction checks how much of an embedding the code preserves. NoteLLM's GCL uses co-reading to decide which content should be close, imposing a different geometry. FineSID trains one backbone first with soft relevance targets and then for personalized CTR. Lower reconstruction error need not improve click ranking, and more plausible LLM output need not match user preferences.

Sources: [Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en.md) · [NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en.md) · [Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Dual-purpose SID and FineSID both use discrete tokens. Why can't a single SID lookup experiment establish both results? {#cross-same-token-different-transfer}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Dual-purpose SID requires codes to support collaborative identity and content reconstruction. FineSID retains fine-grained multiscale positions and transfers the full shared relevance predictor to CTR. A lookup covers only part of the interface. Without reconstruction or stage inheritance respectively, it misses the defining mechanism.

    **Illustrative example:** Using three codes to roughly reconstruct a shoe image is compression. Learning query–shoe relevance and then inheriting the entire interaction network to predict a user's click is a different training pipeline.

    Sources: [Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en.md) · [Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en.md)

### Why can't KAR's generated preference descriptions replace NoteLLM's co-reading supervision? {#cross-generated-knowledge-not-click-label}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** KAR offers candidate knowledge about common sense and preferences; the recommendation objective determines its usefulness. NoteLLM's co-reading pairs come from behavior and directly constrain retrieval geometry. Generated knowledge may fill semantic gaps or invent false explanations. Behavioral pairs are observed but affected by exposure and popularity. They complement one another and are not interchangeable ground truths.

    **Illustrative example:** An LLM's suggestion that campers might like hiking boots is a knowledge hypothesis. Users actually reading about a shoe and waterproof socks together is a platform behavioral relation. The evidence differs.

    Sources: [Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en.md) · [NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en.md)

### Why can recommendation NDCG drop even when SID reconstruction is more accurate and text generation is more fluent? {#cross-reconstruction-versus-preference}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Reconstruction preserves content and CSFT preserves the generation interface, but ranking also needs collaborative distinctions among user–item pairs. A dual-purpose SID codebook may favor content at the expense of preferences; NoteLLM uses GCL for behavior geometry; FineSID continues personalized CTR training. Evaluate reconstruction, collisions, relevance, and isolated test ranking separately.

    **Illustrative example:** Two visually similar coats may be reconstructed accurately, but one is for cycling and the other for commuting. Visual fidelity does not guarantee a correct click order if codes lose the differences between audiences.

    Sources: [Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems](../../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en.md) · [NoteLLM: A Retrievable Large Language Model for Note Recommendation](../../../../reproductions/2403.01744-notellm/README-en.md) · [Progressive Learning from Content to Relevance to Personalization for CTR Prediction](../../../../recommendation-components/2610.29138-finesid/README-en.md)
